name: Multitap
definition: unit that adds controller ports to a console.

name: Cheat device
definition: cartridge or unit that alters a game (Game Genie type).

name: Replacement part or repair tool
definition: spare part or tool for repairing a game machine or controller.

name: Flight stick
definition: joystick controller for flight games.

name: Faceplate, skin or decal
definition: cover plate, skin or decal that changes the outside of one game machine or controller.

name: Toys-to-Life portal or reader
definition: portal or reader that reads Toys-to-Life figures for a game.

name: Hardware upgrade add-on
definition: Unit that plugs into a console to add processors, graphics or memory hardware so that it runs games made for the upgraded system (32X type).

name: Network or modem adapter made for one console
definition: Adapter that adds a dial-up modem, broadband or wireless network connection to one console through its own port or bay; a standard USB network adapter is D1.

name: Game microphone
definition: Microphone made and sold to plug into a console as game input, for singing or voice commands (SingStar type); a headset is D3 and a speech microphone sold for computers is D1.

name: Media add-on made for one console
definition: Remote control, playback kit or TV tuner made to add disc, video or TV functions to one console.

name: Console mouse
definition: Mouse or trackball made to plug into one console as pointing input; a mouse with a standard connector sold for computers is D1.

name: Keyboard made for one console
definition: Keyboard made to plug into one console for typing, programming or text entry in games; a keyboard with a standard connector is D1.

name: Paddle or spinner controller
definition: Controller with a rotary knob whose turn sets a position on screen (paddle, spinner, Vaus type).

name: Phone VR viewer
definition: Headset that encloses the eyes and holds a phone as its display and compute (Cardboard, Gear VR type).

name: Rumble pack
definition: Add-on that plugs into one console's controller to make it vibrate (Rumble Pak, Jump Pack, Vibration Pack).

name: Arcade system board
definition: Circuit board, with its game ROMs, cartridge or disc slot, that runs games inside a coin-operated video cabinet (JAMMA, Naomi, Atomiswave, MVS type).

name: Controller converter
definition: Dongle, adapter or board that translates a controller's signals so it works on a console or computer it was not made for (Brook Wingman, Mayflash Magic type); a plain cable is D5.5.07 or D1.

name: Gear shifter
definition: Lever controller sold apart from a wheel that changes gear in driving games (H-pattern or sequential).

name: Handbrake controller
definition: Lever controller sold apart from a wheel that works the handbrake in driving games.

name: Racing wheelbase
definition: Force-feedback motor base sold without a rim, onto which interchangeable rims mount by a quick release; drive type (direct, belt, gear) is an attribute.

name: Tabletop electronic game
definition: Dedicated game machine with its game built in and its own screen (VFD, LCD or LED), made to stand on a table, not held and not linked to a TV.

name: Cooling unit made for one console
definition: External fan, cooling stand or clip-on unit made to cool one console; a replacement internal fan is D5.5.13.

name: Flight yoke
definition: controller with a yoke handle on a column that pushes, pulls and turns, made for flying aircraft in games and simulators; sold alone or packed with a throttle.

name: Flight throttle
definition: lever unit sold apart from a stick or yoke that sets engine power, often with flap or trim levers, in flight games and simulators; a stick-and-throttle set (HOTAS) is a flight stick.

name: Sim cockpit or wheel stand
definition: frame, stand or seat rig made to hold a racing wheel, pedals, shifter or flight controls for play; a gaming chair without controller mounts is B1.
